leah: Noticed reproducible divergence on nightlies for 'skua-9b:int4' after ~9.6k tokens. Keys stop matching earlier snapshots.
sam: any diffs in raw kv key bytes?
leah: yes, ran byte-dump: key bytes before 9600 show expected prefix 'ab cd ef', after 9600 they appear byte-reversed 'ef cd ab'.
omar: byte-reversed? sounds like endianness flip during pack/unpack crossing CPU/GPU boundary. Did we change memcpy or vectorized store path for compact int4?
leah: recent patch switched host packing to a vectorized 32-bit lane store; on little-endian hosts that can change byte layout for the tiny-pair packing. Kernel assumed contiguous byte order. On certain drivers the alignment pad combined with the new store changes per-word ordering.
sam: can you paste small dump and repro?
leah: ```
# reproduce
./run_eval.sh --model skua-9b:int4 --prompt tests/repro/endian_flip.json --max-tokens 12000

# dump
kv_key[9598]=0x'ab cd ef 01 23 45'
kv_key[9599]=0x'ef cd ab 01 23 45'  <-- reversed
```
ci-bot: [run 2026-05-12T06:01:00Z] scheduled reproduce-endian (id: 3344)
omar: hypothesis: vectorized store + PR#4988 extra shift create a per-word byte flip when index crosses 9600 due to an alignment pad.
leah: quick mitigation: normalize byte order explicitly in the host packer (htonl/ntohl) before device transfer and add a unit test that asserts kv key bytes equal after roundtrip. Opening PR.
leah: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7012 - byte-order normalization + regression test
sam: deployed to canary; rerun shows kv keys consistent and generation matches baseline through 12k. loss diffs within noise.
omar: add onboarding note: when enabling SIMD/vectorized host packing, assert canonical byte-order and alignment across kernel ABIs. Add nightly byte-level kv parity check.
leah: will add metric kv.byte_parity_fail_count and alert if >0. thanks all :sparkles:
